question: Which native hook observability shape should remain open for the Codex relay fan-out investigation: this timing-log PR, the aggregate relay-metrics PR, or a split/narrowed combination?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102241 instrument overlapping relay investigation paths, while this PR also broadens diagnostics into the generic plugin hook runner; choosing that permanent diagnostic shape is an operations/product judgment rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Prefer aggregate metrics after proof
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102241 as the main relay observability lane once it has redacted real-run proof, and split only the generic plugin handler timing from this PR if maintainers still want it.

options.title: Keep this timing PR
options.body: Ask the sibling aggregate-metrics PR to close or narrow if maintainers prefer per-invocation and per-handler timing logs over aggregate unregister summaries.

options.title: Pause both instrumentation PRs
options.body: Wait until the broader behavior mitigation path for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91009 is chosen, then add only the diagnostics that mitigation still needs.

recommendation.title: Prefer aggregate metrics after proof
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102241 as the main relay observability lane once it has redacted real-run proof, and split only the generic plugin handler timing from this PR if maintainers still want it.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the current relay and hook-runner implementations makes this the strongest routing candidate for choosing the observability shape.
